subsystems.name: Recognition layer
subsystems.role: decides what is 'self' and what is foreign, molecule by molecule.
parts: affinity ligands such as antibodies, aptamers or engineered receptor proteins
surface patterning that presents many ligands at once
amplification chemistry so a single binding event produces a signal

subsystems.name: Decision logic
subsystems.role: turns binding signals into a yes/no action without a human in the loop.
parts: DNA or RNA strand-displacement circuits
threshold gates that require several markers before firing
a built-in timer so the device deactivates after a set time

subsystems.name: Effector payload
subsystems.role: neutralises whatever the logic has flagged.
parts: antimicrobial peptides
nucleases that cut nucleic acids
neutralising proteins that block binding to host cells
membrane-disrupting or toxin-absorbing particles

subsystems.name: Chassis and body
subsystems.role: the physical container that carries the payload and survives in blood.
parts: lipid nanoparticle
DNA-origami or protein cage scaffold
polymer shell with a stealth coating
attachment points for ligands and payloads

subsystems.name: Power and propulsion
subsystems.role: lets the particle reach tissue rather than circulating passively.
parts: chemical energy from glucose or ATP in the blood
magnetic or ultrasound guidance from outside the body
gradient-following movement toward inflammation signals

subsystems.name: Clearance and safety controls
subsystems.role: ensures the device leaves the body and cannot be hijacked.
parts: biodegradable bonds with a defined half-life
kidney-clearable size design
a kill switch triggered by an external dose of a small molecule

buildSteps.title: Choose the chassis
buildSteps.detail: Pick a carrier — lipid nanoparticle, DNA-origami cage or polymer shell — sized below roughly 100 nm so it circulates and eventually clears through the kidneys.

buildSteps.title: Screen the recognition molecules
buildSteps.detail: Generate candidate binders against a target pathogen surface using library methods such as phage display, then measure their affinity and cross-reactivity against human proteins.

buildSteps.title: Wire the logic circuit
buildSteps.detail: Assemble nucleic-acid strands that fire only when two or three distinct foreign markers are present, so the device does not attack healthy tissue.

buildSteps.title: Load the effector
buildSteps.detail: Attach peptides, nucleases or neutralising proteins at a controlled ratio, then verify that the payload stays inert until the logic gate opens.

buildSteps.title: Add stealth and safety
buildSteps.detail: Coat the surface to slow clearance by the liver and spleen, and include a degradation timer so activity fades within days.

buildSteps.title: Test in human plasma and organ models
buildSteps.detail: Measure killing of the target pathogen in blood, plasma and tissue cultures, and check for effects on red cells, clotting and normal immune cells.

buildSteps.title: Animal studies
buildSteps.detail: Assess how long the particles persist, where they accumulate, and whether they reduce infection in living animals.

buildSteps.title: Clinical trials
buildSteps.detail: Run phased human trials for safety first, then for effectiveness against one specific pathogen — not a universal claim.

buildSteps.title: Manufacture and dose
buildSteps.detail: Produce batches under pharmaceutical quality control and administer by infusion at intervals, because the devices are cleared and must be replaced.

prerequisites.why: antibodies and aptamers already distinguish targets with high specificity, which is the sensing foundation.
DNA strand-displacement circuits work in test tubes and simple cellular settings, but not yet reliably inside a circulating particle in blood.
lipid nanoparticles are already produced at scale for mRNA medicines, giving a real manufacturing base.

prerequisites.tech: Nanoscale power and actuation inside the body
prerequisites.why: there is no proven way for a free-floating particle to generate its own movement or do mechanical work for long.
rules are built around fixed molecules, not devices whose behaviour depends on a logic circuit.

pathway.milestone: nanoparticle delivery systems and engineered cell therapies in the clinic
pathway.unlocks: a proven base of materials, manufacturing and safety data.

pathway.milestone: multifunctional particles that both detect a marker and release a drug in response
pathway.unlocks: the first closed-loop, sense-and-act therapeutics in trials.

pathway.milestone: implanted or infused synthetic gene circuits in living cells that respond to infection
pathway.unlocks: programmable defence without removing the patient's own immune system.

pathway.milestone: injectable nanoscale agents giving weeks of added immune protection
pathway.unlocks: a supplement to the immune system for outbreaks or immunocompromised patients.
